title: Construction Contract Performance Guarantees 2026: 2–10% and Refund
desc: Construction contract performance guarantees 2026: security measures, 2%-10% of contract value, when a contractor forfeits it and when it is returned.
summary: The security measures for construction contract performance under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 210/2026/ND-CP, the 2%–10% level and the cases in which a contractor does not get the security back.
body: p

A performance guarantee is a "cushion" that keeps the homeowner or project owner from losing everything when a contractor abandons, delays or botches the contract. This article summarises the rules in Article 83 of the Construction Law 2025 and Article 13 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP (effective 1 July 2026).
h2
1. What does contract performance security include?
p

For public-investment and PPP projects, security for obligations under a construction contract includes: performance security, payment security, advance payment guarantee and warranty security. The measure may be a guarantee, a deposit or another measure under law; the parties give priority to guarantees (Points a and b, Clause 2, Article 13). The Civil Code lists 9 security measures, including deposit, escrow and guarantee (Article 292).
p

A guarantee is where a third party (usually a bank) undertakes to perform the obligation in place of the contractor if the contractor fails to perform or performs improperly (Article 335 of the Civil Code).
h2
2. Each party's right to require security
ul
The parties may agree on a security measure; once agreed, it must be maintained until the obligation is completed or the security is returned (Clause 1, Article 83 of the Construction Law).

The employer may require the contractor to provide performance security, and may enforce the security asset or require the bank to pay in its place when the contractor's breach compromises safety, quality or progress or the contractor refuses to perform the contract (Clause 2).
Conversely, the contractor may require the employer to prove adequate financial capacity or to provide payment security, except for contracts in public-investment projects (Clause 3).
p
For a house funded by a household itself, whether there is a guarantee and its amount are for the two parties to agree.
h2
3. Level of performance security
p

For public-investment and PPP projects, performance security is from 2% to 10% of the contract value; if a level above 10% is wanted to guard against risk, the procurement law applies (Point dd, Clause 2, Article 13; Clause 4, Article 68 of the Law on Bidding). Some cases require no security, such as consulting contractors, self-performing contractors or community participation in implementation (Clause 2, Article 68).
p
For a joint-venture contractor, each member provides security corresponding to its own portion of work, or the lead member provides it if so agreed (Point h, Clause 2, Article 13).
h2
4. When does the contractor forfeit the security?
p
The contractor does not get back the performance security when (Point dd, Clause 2, Article 13):
ul
It refuses to perform the contract after the contract has taken effect;
It is behind schedule through its own fault but refuses to extend the validity of the security;
Other breaches serious enough that the security is to be forfeited under the contract.
h2
5. When is the security returned?
ul

The employer returns the performance security after the contractor has completed all obligations, or has moved on to the warranty obligation and the employer has received the warranty security (for work subject to warranty).
Warranty security is returned only after the warranty period ends and the employer confirms that the warranty has been completed (Point g, Clause 2, Article 13).
If escrow is used, or the employer retains money from payments as security, the contractor is entitled to the interest arising on that amount (Point b, Clause 2, Article 13).
h2
6. Notes for homeowners
ol
State clearly in the contract: the type of security, the level (% or amount), the validity period and the cases in which it is forfeited.
If the schedule is extended, require the contractor to extend the guarantee accordingly.
Retaining part of each payment is also a form of security, but state clearly when it will be returned.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The 2%–10% level and the cases of forfeiture and return of security in Decree 210/2026/ND-CP are rules for public-investment and PPP projects; for private works, the parties agree. The Law on Bidding 2023 is currently partially no longer in effect. For contracts signed and being performed before 1 July 2026 (projects not using public-investment capital), the parties may agree to apply Decree 210/2026/ND-CP; if they cannot agree, the rules at the time of signing apply (Clause 2, Article 33).
